Maybe this is out of subject, but in reality does it matter what mag capacity that you are loading it? I mean logically the mag spring for big mags must be bigger but does it really matter? lets say you have two 5.56 mags one is 30 round the other is 40 or 100.

I never have held a mag in real life which is why am curious.

comments.author: JackBrush
comments.body_html:
I haven’t used drum magazines myself but age of the magazine spring can make loading even lower capacity magazines like my beretta 18rd mags very hard for the last couple of rounds.

There are different mechanisms when it comes to drum mags. I’ve seen windup magazines that you load first then turn a handle to adjust the spring tension, drums in which you open up and drop the rounds in, and drums without these features that seemingly just use a normal design you would see with box magazines.

I don’t think that they would necessarily be harder to load though, particularly broken in (well used) magazine springs. What you see in Tarkov is just balance. If you could load a drum mag as fast as a 30 round box mag, why would you use box magazines?

Anyway we’re playing offline so I don’t see any reason for the nerf.
